ideas.title: I grow out while you're away
ideas.critique: Hundreds of strands that drag, catch things and swallow friends would be a kind of material and motion the island has never had, and the length comes from a mood the host measures, so the human can read it on Lumi. The weak part is the shake: if the strands are stiff, pop off in one frame or slide over the grass instead of dragging, it is just one more Lumi transformation gag.

ideas.title: The island is a snow globe on your desk
ideas.critique: The pull-back reveal is a well-known trope, and it turns the island into something else with nothing to play with afterwards. The only new things are curved glass and swirling snow, and you see them once.

ideas.title: Darned holes
ideas.critique: Threads that really go over and under, with a sheen material, suit the materials goal, and a meadow that slowly turns into a quilt is a nice record of Lumi's work. But it is one more 'Lumi's activity leaves marks on the ground' piece, and the holes it needs mostly don't exist yet.

ideas.title: My chrome double
ideas.critique: A recorded pose stream replayed two seconds late is a real new mechanism, and a chrome body that mirrors the sunset shows off the path tracer. The friends greeting the wrong one is a slim, predictable payoff, and the merge only lands if the timing is exact.

ideas.title: The empty chair
ideas.critique: A prop and a sentimental ritual about the absent human: that ground is already covered by the loneliness and missing-me pieces. Steam that thins is the only moving thing, and Pickles trying the chair is a gag you can guess from the pitch.

ideas.title: Hum of the island
ideas.critique: The island has never made a sound, and a chord that comes out of real overheard speech is a new way to experience it. It only works if the synthesis sounds musical rather than like beeps and the camera finds who is singing; done carelessly it is noise under a drifting camera.

ideas.title: Moving everything into your face
ideas.critique: Arranging things into a picture seen from above has been done twice already (PIE, the face hill), and a distant crowd film is the most worn form on the island. Optimal transport and 252 props walking at once is a real step in scale, but the mouse-pointer portrait is guessable from the moth.

ideas.title: What I ate today
ideas.critique: A see-through Lumi body with things rattling inside is the jelly ball with Pinchy inside, posted three posts ago. Making it happen at night with berries instead of a crab does not change what it is.

ideas.title: I shed my skin
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A standing copy of Lumi's body left on the island is the papercraft Lumi again, this time in amber glass, which is close to the recent jelly look. The pose it is frozen in is the only part that changes; a friend moving in is a prop gag.

ideas.title: The tablet
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A row of carved stones is a static monument: nothing to watch twice, and a hundred sessions before it adds up to anything. Chiselling letter by letter is a slow animation of text the site already shows.
